clue.text: Good behaviour code broken with arrival of drink

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of the word code are rearranged

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a strong drink

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct goes out of the window once the bottle appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' scrambles CODE into DECO; 'with arrival of' joins the drink RUM on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is propriety, the seemly conduct expected in polite company.

clue.text: Composer's name not encountered in Sussex area?

indicators.note: something not encountered is missing from the scene, so one letter drops out of the Sussex word

parts.note: the South Downs of Sussex are chalk downland

explanation.surface: Asking which composer's name never cropped up in a corner of southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not encountered' removes N (name) from DOWNLAND, the rolling chalk hills of Sussex, leaving DOWLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dowland was an English Renaissance composer of lute songs.

clue.text: Clergymen antagonistic about new scripture reference

parts.note: a cathedral chapter is the body of its clergy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for antagonistic goes round the letter for new

parts.note: adverse means hostile or opposed

explanation.surface: Hostile clerics quarrel over a fresh citation from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clergymen' are a cathedral chapter, its governing body of canons, not individual priests.
explanation.definitionFit: Citing chapter and verse means giving the exact location of a passage in the Bible.

clue.text: Odd parts of rougher industrial area

indicators.note: the odd parts are the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Bits of a rougher region known for heavy industry.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of ROUGHER gives R, U, H, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr is Germany's great coal and steel region.

clue.text: Notice endless pleasure embracing right girl

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to mark something is to notice it

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the pleasure word wraps round the letter

parts.note: joy is great pleasure

explanation.surface: Spotting unending delight as one hugs the correct young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Marjory is a female first name.

clue.text: Call to ditch new transport for one in flying chariot

indicators.note: to ditch is to get rid of, so a letter is thrown out of the call word

parts.note: to phone someone is to call them
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: Someone rings to scrap a new vehicle in favour of an airborne carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in flying chariot' is the sun god, said to drive the sun across the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebus Apollo, the Greek sun god, was pictured driving the sun's chariot across the sky.

clue.text: Firm turning up in media mechanism

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the media word

parts.note: the press is the news media

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company appears in the newspapers as a piece of machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads the firm's letters from the bottom, so they come out reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is a method or procedure by which something works.

clue.text: Nothing to constrain Parliament's welcoming attitude

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pen is to confine or shut in
a house, such as the House of Commons, is a chamber of Parliament

explanation.surface: Nothing holds back the legislature's hospitable approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to constrain' looks like a containment instruction but simply gives PEN as a piece of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping open house means always being hospitable to visitors.

clue.text: Comprehensive approach afforded by duvet?

explanation.surface: A wide-ranging strategy compared to what a bedspread provides.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the phrase literally: a duvet is a quilt that gives the cover of a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: Total, all-inclusive treatment of a subject is called this, and a quilt literally provides bedclothes cover.

clue.text: Gratify composer, bringing in a lead from trombones

indicators.note: bringing in means taking inside, so the composer's name encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Erik Satie was a French composer

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Pleasing a musician by bringing in a solo from the brass section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing in' puts A and T (first of trombones) inside SATIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy fully, filling an appetite.

clue.text: It could be revised after a shower, etc

definitions.text: It could be revised after a shower, etc

indicators.note: revised means altered and reworked, so the letters that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prediction that may need changing once rain has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' rearranges AFTERASHOWERETC; and a forecast is just the sort of thing updated after unexpected rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A meteorological prediction is often revised when rain arrives that it did not foresee.

clue.text: Article on money and perverted love -it has no real storyline

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
tin is slang for money

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of shape, so the letters of love are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grammar, cash and twisted romance make up a book without a plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' and 'and' only join the pieces; 'tin' as money is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-novel is an experimental work of fiction that rejects conventional plot and character.

clue.text: See 10
Bird that's returned when going round this country

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the whole assembly is read backwards to give the bird
going round means encircling, so the reversed word surrounds the country

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
UK, the United Kingdom, is the setter's own country

explanation.surface: A bird that has flown back and is circling Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns the whole bird, AUKS, round; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The skua is a predatory seabird.

clue.text: Boxer's weakness-clashing's out

indicators.note: out means not in order, so the letters of clashing's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter's vulnerability is that he is no longer brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CLASHINGS; the apostrophe adds nothing, its S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer who is easily knocked out is said to have a fragile jaw of this kind.

clue.text: See 6
Queen's consort to repair meadow

parts.note: to darn is to mend a hole in fabric
a ley is a field of grass, a meadow

explanation.surface: A royal husband is told to mend the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen is Mary Queen of Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Darnley was the second husband of Mary Queen of Scots.

clue.text: Dog's bed included mostly

annotationWithheld.why: 'Dog's bed included mostly' (7) as held: SCOTTIE is S + COT + TIE or COT inside STIE(S), but no word here gives the surrounding letters; a word looks lost in OCR and no reprint found

clue.text: Wager about individual's work in hospital?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wager word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a bet is a wager
ones are individuals, with the 's read as a plural

explanation.surface: Betting on a person's job on the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads the plant name literally as setting bones, a hospital job.
explanation.definitionFit: Boneset is a herb once used to help fractures heal; the question mark flags reading it as orthopaedic surgery.

clue.text: Man with whaling captain turning up in exotic islands

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
Ahab is the whaling captain in Moby-Dick

explanation.surface: A fellow sails with a famous whaler to faraway islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses SAMAHAB as a whole, giving BAHAMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bahamas are an archipelago in the Caribbean region.

clue.text: Dry spell initially occupying days in June

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so the letter goes into the number word

parts.note: June has thirty days

indicators.note: initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A dry spell holding through June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes S from spell; 'occupying' puts it inside THIRTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty means wanting a drink, parched.

clue.text: Male covering fool in vestment

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the male word encloses the fool

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A man throws his coat over an idiot in church robes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is a long garment worn by clergy.

clue.text: Drug bearing obscure writing in English

parts.note: a code is writing made deliberately unclear

explanation.surface: A medicine bearing cryptic text in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Codeine is a painkilling opiate.

clue.text: What should precede this insect in book?

definitions.text: What should precede this insect in book?

parts.words: What should precede this insect in book?
parts.note: put the word 'What' before the insect's name and you have the title of a children's book by Susan Coolidge

explanation.surface: Asking which word comes before an insect in a book's title.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'What' is part of the title, What Katy Did.
explanation.definitionFit: The katydid is a North American bush cricket named for its call.

clue.text: Curtailment of rash example of activity

indicators.note: curtailment means cutting off the tail, the last letter

parts.note: hives is an itchy rash

explanation.surface: Cutting short a rash in a busy place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtailment of' drops the final S of HIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy place is called a hive of activity, the fullest example of bustle.

clue.text: Chopped rinds in cream — constituent of soup?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the chopped letters go within the cream word

parts.note: the cream is the best part

indicators.note: chopped means cut up, so the letters of rinds are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe step: chopped rind folded into cream for a soup.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird's nest soup is a Chinese delicacy made from swiftlet nests, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible swiftlet nests are the main ingredient of a Chinese delicacy soup.

clue.text: See 22
See 13
Dirt's filling Thames slowly

indicators.note: filling means sitting inside, so the answer is found within the words

explanation.surface: Pollution seeping into the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across thaMES Slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is something dirty or untidy.

clue.text: US resort mart heavy rains'd spoil?

indicators.note: spoil means ruin, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Asking whether torrential rain would ruin a market at an American holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoil' rearranges the letters of heavy rains'd after MART, which stays as it is; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha's Vineyard is an island holiday destination off Massachusetts.

clue.text: Cunning traps bird without relenting

indicators.note: traps means catches inside, so the cunning word encloses the bird

parts.note: sly means cunning
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A crafty catcher snares a bird without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting sternly means severely and unyieldingly.

clue.text: Man carrying a gun in part of London

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the man's name encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Ed is a man's name
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A man with a weapon in a part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditionally working-class area of London east of the City.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is a district of east London.
